title: The condensed ring $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell$
statement:
For a prime $\ell$, the condensed ring $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell$ is the condensed ring
$\underline T$ of [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring] for $T=\mathbf Z_\ell$ ([def-weil-l-adic-numbers]) with the
$\ell$-adic topology:

$$
\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell(S)=C(S,\mathbf Z_\ell).
$$

Its underlying ring object of $\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ is commutative.

proof.text: By [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], $\mathbf Z_\ell=\{x\in\mathbf Q_\ell:|x|_\ell\le1\}$ in the nonarchimedean valued field $\mathbf Q_\ell$. The inequalities $|x+y|_\ell\le\max(|x|_\ell,|y|_\ell)$, $|xy|_\ell=|x|_\ell|y|_\ell$, and $|-x|_\ell=|x|_\ell$ show that it is a subring, hence commutative. For $x,y,x\prime,y\prime\in\mathbf Z_\ell$, they also give $|(x+y)-(x\prime+y\prime)|_\ell\le\max(|x-x\prime|_\ell,|y-y\prime|_\ell)$ and $|xy-x\prime y\prime|_\ell\le\max(|x-x\prime|_\ell,|y-y\prime|_\ell)$, using $xy-x\prime y\prime=x(y-y\prime)+(x-x\prime)y\prime$ and the norm bounds by $1$. Negation is an isometry, so all ring operations are continuous for the restricted metric. For $a\in\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $n\ge0$, one has $|x-a|_\ell\le\ell^{-n}$ if and only if $x=a+\ell^n z$ with $z\in\mathbf Z_\ell$: take $z=(x-a)/\ell^n$ and use $|\ell|_\ell=\ell^{-1}$. Hence these balls are precisely $a+\ell^n\mathbf Z_\ell$. Each is open by the ultrametric inequality (a ball of strict radius $\ell^{-n}$ about any of its points stays inside it), and their radii tend to zero because $\ell\ge2$. They therefore form a neighbourhood basis for the restricted metric as well as the adic topology. Thus this topology is exactly the $\ell$-adic topology and $\mathbf Z_\ell$ is a commutative topological ring.

source.place: the sole proof sentence; expanded verification of the topological-ring hypothesis

proof.text: Apply [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring] to the commutative topological ring $T=\mathbf Z_\ell$ from step 1. It gives a sheaf of rings with sections $C(S,\mathbf Z_\ell)$, restriction along $u:S\prime\to S$ given by $a\mapsto a\circ u$, and pointwise operations; define $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell$ to be this sheaf. The same cited statement says that its underlying ring object in $\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ is commutative when $T$ is commutative, which step 1 verified.
